blurb: Pixie-faced English cat with huge ears and a short, rippled curly coat
description: The Devon Rex is a short-haired cat breed from Devon, England, with a medium build, large wide-set ears, big eyes and a soft, wavy curled coat.
answer: The Devon Rex is a short-haired domestic cat breed that emerged in Devon, England, around 1960. It has a medium build, an elfin wedge-shaped head with very large ears and eyes, and a soft coat that curls into waves.

body: The breed traces back to a curly-coated kitten named Kirlee, found by Beryl Cox in Buckfastleigh, Devon, in 1960. Cox first assumed Kirlee carried the same gene as the Cornish Rex and bred him to Cornish Rexes, but the resulting kittens all had straight coats. This showed that Kirlee carried a different mutation, and Cox began a breeding program to preserve it.

The Devon Rex is a very short-haired cat of medium build with a head type often described as pixie-like: a short, broad wedge with a curving brow and flat skull. The eyes are large, oval and set wide, and may be any color. The ears are large, wide-set and round-tipped. The coat is short, dense and soft and curls inward to give a waved or rippled look, though areas such as the neck may be too sparsely furred to show the ripple. Whiskers and eyebrows are crinkled, and any coat color is allowed.

The source material used here says little about the breed's personality. As with any breed, individual temperament varies, and owners are best guided by meeting cats and by descriptions from breed clubs.

Sources give little specific care detail. Because the coat is short and in places sparse, owners generally handle it gently; routine care such as play, a clean environment and regular veterinary check-ups applies as for any cat.

Conditions reported in the breed include a hereditary myopathy linked to a COLQ genetic variant, which can appear between 3 and 23 weeks of age, as well as feline atopic dermatitis, congenital hypotrichosis and Malassezia dermatitis. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock.

faq.q: Where does the Devon Rex come from?
faq.a: The breed began in Devon, England, from a curly-coated kitten found in Buckfastleigh in 1960.

faq.q: Is the Devon Rex the same as the Cornish Rex?
faq.a: No. Test breedings showed the Devon Rex curl is caused by a different mutation from the Cornish Rex, since crosses between the two produced straight-coated kittens.

faq.q: What does a Devon Rex coat look like?
faq.a: It is short, dense and soft, curling inward into waves or ripples, with crinkled whiskers and eyebrows; some areas such as the neck can be thinly furred.
